ideas.angle: Grok Bot making phone calls turns a chatbot into something that talks to the real world, and the screenshot is the proof.
ideas.hook_en: Grok Bot called Anthropic at 3am and held for 21 minutes about a Claude limit. AI agents are now doing the phone calls humans hate.
ideas.title: Grok Bot picks up the phone
ideas.visual: Image: the Grok Bot call screenshot with the 21-minute hold time circled, plus the Anthropic call log.
ideas.why: jayypatel18 Grok Bot call post 842,932 views; TheRundownAI Grok Bot phone post 7,684 views.

ideas.angle: IPI Bench measures indirect prompt injection against agents on realistic workplace tasks, the first benchmark built for the way agents actually get attacked.
ideas.hook_en: Prompt injection is now a benchmark, not a warning: IPI Bench tests agents on realistic workplace tasks, and AI agents keep failing the same traps.
ideas.title: Prompt injection now has a benchmark
ideas.visual: Image: the IPI Bench results chart with the worst indirect injection cases highlighted.
ideas.why: gen_analysis IPI Bench post 335,125 views; prompt injection X keyword table rank 5, up x5.19.

ideas.angle: Levelsio's AI-reply fight shows the other side of the agent boom: bots replying to posts faster than humans can block them.
ideas.hook_en: Levelsio still blocks about 50 AI reply accounts a day, and blames Grok access. AI agents are now the spam, and the filters cannot keep up.
ideas.title: AI replies are now the spam
ideas.visual: Image: the levelsio AI-reply post with a count of blocked accounts drawn as a tally.
ideas.why: levelsio AI-reply post 50,512 views, the fourth-biggest watchlist hit of Nov 5; two more AI-reply posts the same day.

ideas.angle: A 23-minute Claude Code tutorial builds four AI agents from scratch, the practical end of the agent hype.
ideas.hook_en: Four AI agents built from scratch with Claude Code in 23 minutes, aimed at $250k of work. Watch the tutorial once, then build your own version.
ideas.title: Four agents from scratch in 23 minutes
ideas.visual: Screencast: the first agent from the tutorial built live, with the four-agent setup on screen.
ideas.why: deanwperkins tutorial post 983,809 views; AI agents X keyword table rank 2, up x1.46.

ideas.angle: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings stronger consistency and 30 percent lower cost to AI video, and GPT-Image-2.6 brings faster image generation to Codex and the API.
ideas.hook_en: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes AI video cheaper and steadier, while Codex gets GPT-Image-2.6. The models are racing on price and speed now, not just quality.
ideas.title: Video and image models race on price
ideas.visual: Video: side-by-side clips from Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash and GPT-Image-2.6 outputs, cut to the same prompt.
ideas.why: Google Gemini Omni post 458,445 views; OpenAIDevs GPT-Image-2.6 post 350,221 views.

ideas.angle: Claude Personal Finance in US beta answers money questions from real balances, read-only, so the model looks but never moves money.
ideas.hook_en: Claude can now answer money questions from your own balances, and ChatGPT cannot do that yet. Personal Finance turns your AI into a read-only money assistant.
ideas.title: Claude answers money questions, read-only
ideas.visual: Video: screen recording of Claude answering a money question from balances, with the read-only badge highlighted.
ideas.why: claudeai Personal Finance post 4,614,355 views, the biggest outsider of Nov 5.

ideas.angle: Living Brain gives one persistent memory to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Codex and own agents, with 92.2 percent on LoCoMo and 464ms retrieval.
ideas.hook_en: Your ChatGPT should remember you when you switch to Claude. Living Brain is one memory layer across models, and the LLM stops starting from zero.
ideas.title: One memory for every model you use
ideas.visual: Video: same question asked in ChatGPT, then Claude, then Codex, with the same memory answering each time.
ideas.why: ladyxtel Living Brain post 4,552,981 views, second-biggest outsider of Nov 5; repeat from the Nov 4 board at 1,702,090 views.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
